title: Engine Room Ops Snapshot — Orthogonal Incidents & Handoffs (week of 2027-02-15)
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact, engineer-forward weekly snapshot intended for the on-call rotation, SRE standups, and product stakeholders who want a quick read on reliability posture. Focus this week: an orthogonal set of smaller incidents that collectively impacted latency SLOs and increased paging noise.

Summary (one-liner):
- Multiple small, loosely-related incidents (KV cache eviction pattern + monitoring flapping + an automated circuit-breaker cascade) caused a transient p95 latency SLO breach on 2027-02-18 for ~70 minutes. No data loss, fallbacks triggered.

Timeline & Standup Logs (brief):
Mon 2027-02-15
- 09:30 standup: prep for synthetic load test; note: canary traffic enabled on staging.
- Evening: low-priority alert from synthetic job about higher tail latency on a staging shard (ticketed but triaged low).

Tue 2027-02-16
- 11:00: engineering sync with infra: rolling kernel update scheduled for dedicated nodes next week. No immediate ops impact.
- 16:00: small spike in cache-miss rate observed (KV cache TTL churn on one pool). Logged for follow-up.

Wed 2027-02-17
- 07:15 on-call: transient circuit-breaker trips reported by runtime when a downstream telemetry endpoint timed out. Circuit opened for ~8m and rate-limited a small percentage of inference requests; fallbacks used successfully.
- 14:00: post-incident quick retro: root cause unknown — assigned SRE-8421.

Thu 2027-02-18 (main composite event)
- 02:50: monitoring flapping began (Prometheus alert flapped from OK->WARN->OK across multiple targets). Cause: exporter restart loop on telemetry aggregation host (OOM during a short memory spike).
- 03:05: concurrent KV cache eviction anomaly on the prefix-cache: eviction storm + re-warm caused severe KV miss amplification.
- 03:12: circuit-breaker in front of a lower-tier model variant began tripping; the routing layer routed to higher-latency fallback model causing p95 to rise.
- 03:18: automated mitigation: routing layer enacted canary fallback policy (graceful degrade to smaller batch sizes, prefetched KV warm calls).
- 04:30: all systems restored to baseline; p95 SLO considered recovered. Post-mortem meeting scheduled.

Fri 2027-02-19
- 10:00: incident review; quick fixes deployed (exporter restart backoff tuning, cache rewarm pacing, circuit-breaker threshold adjustment).
- 15:00: ops runbook updates drafted; canary config tightened for fallback routing.

SLO status & metrics snapshot (high level):
- latency.p95.prod: SLO = 200ms, breach window 03:05–04:15 on 2027-02-18 (approx 70 mins). Root contributors: cache-miss amplification (≈55%), fallback routing to slower model (≈30%), exporter flapping noise (≈15%).
- errors.rate.prod: spike to 0.8% (baseline 0.12%) during the window; mostly 5xx originating from the telemetry proxy that then cascaded to circuit-breaker logic.
- availability.prod: no sustained unavailability; no customer-facing downtime.

Incidents (short notes & status):
- SRE-8421: "KV eviction amplification + routing fallback" — status: in_progress. Owner: Ravi Patel. Next step: run replay to reproduce eviction storm and test rewarm pacing.
- SRE-8430: "Telemetry exporter restart loop" — status: resolved (hotfix backoff change). Owner: Marta López. Follow-up: longer-term memory cap and load-shedding for exporter.
- SRE-8435: "Circuit-breaker tuning caused extra failover" — status: in_review. Owner: Connor Ng. PR opened to add a short jitter and lower aggressiveness for model-variant circuit-breakers.

On-call handoff notes (for next shift):
- Pagermix: expect elevated noise on telemetry exporter alerts until backoff fully rolled out. Suppress non-actionable exporter flaps with alert throttling rule (temp).
- If p95 spikes: check cache miss dashboard -> "prefix-eviction-rate" panel and warm job queue length. If both high, trigger manual cache-throttle (playbook section 2.1).
- Circuit-breaker events: confirm whether fallback routing is the root or a downstream latency — use tracing tag rb.circuit_origin to correlate.
- Contact list: Ravi (pager), Marta (pager), Connor (secondary).

Operational decisions made this week:
- Short-term: deploy exporter backoff patch to all telemetry hosts (rolled 03:56 on 02/18). Add alert dedupe for exporter flaps (threshold to 3 occurrences in 5m).
- Mid-term: implement cache rewarm pacing (limit warming concurrency to 10/warm job). Prototype in staging next week.
- Long-term: revisit circuit-breaker policy for model routing — adding hysteresis and randomized recovery window. Track effect with synthetic canary tests.

Runbook & Playbook changes (drafted):
- Add a new checklist: "Eviction storm triage" (detect, pause traffic to affected prefix, start controlled rewarm).
- Add recommended default for circuit-breaker: minOpenTime=30s, recovery-jitter=up_to_10s.
- Add a note to synthetic traffic jobs to include a slow-path variant so fallbacks are exercised in canary windows.

Action items (owner — ETA):
- Ravi: reproduce eviction pattern in replay harness; propose rewarm concurrency limit — ETA 2027-02-25.
- Marta: finalize exporter memory cap + backoff design doc and schedule capacity test — ETA 2027-03-02.
- Connor: land PR for circuit-breaker jitter and roll to canary — ETA 2027-02-24.
- Ava: update runbook and publish playbook changes, send short comms to product teams summarizing impact — ETA 2027-02-23.

Open questions / unresolved:
- Why did the cache TTL churn happen on that particular pool? Hypothesis: a scheduled background job overlapped with rebalancing — need to inspect recent control-plane ops.
- Are telemetry exporter restarts masking real downstream errors? Need deeper tracing correlation to confirm.

Misc small notes (scratchpad style):
- Observed a ~2% increase in burst token cost during the event due to rerouted higher-latency model usage — economics note for Optimize team.
- Suggest adding smoke tests that assert "no more than 10% of traffic should flip to fallback under synthetic moderate load".
- Quick comms draft to Growth/Product: short bullet explaining no customer-facing downtime; proactive mitigations in progress.

Meeting notes from post-incident retro (2027-02-19):
- What went well: fallback routing prevented errors from reaching customers; automated canary begin rollback worked.
- What to improve: alert correlation and dedupe; clearer on-call runbook steps for eviction storms.
- Actionable: add a visual "circuit-breaker heatmap" to on-call dashboard (owner: Connor).

Appendix (links & snippets):
- Short trace id for one sample flowed during the event: trace: 7f3a2b9c — use to correlate logs (SRE-8421).
- Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1293 (circuit-breaker jitter).
- Jira: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/SRE-8421 (main incident), https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/SRE-8430 (exporter), https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/SRE-8435 (circuit-breaker tuning).

If you're reading this as the next on-call: skim Summary + On-call handoff notes first, then see Action items to know what will land during your shift. Leave notes in the doc (append at bottom) with your initials and timestamp.

-- Ava T. (SRE rotation lead this week)
